steps.description:
In this exercise, you will learn a Python built-in function isdigit(). It will be used at the last step of this challenge.

You can check if a variable contains only digits using the isdigit() function.

For example, given text="123" , then text.isdigit() returns True because it contains only digits. Otherwise, it will return False.

Write a program to ask user input a string and display "all are digits" if it contains only digits. Otherwise, display "not all are digits".

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input

1234567890

abc100

-999

5.55

5 5

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the example below:

Example 1 Enter string: 1234567890 all are digits

Example 2 Enter string: abc100 not all are digits

Example 3 Enter string: -999 not all are digits

Example 4 Enter string: 5.55 not all are digits

Example 5 Enter string: 5 5 not all are digits

In this exercise, you will learn a Python built-in function find(). It will be used at the last step of this challenge.

You can find the existence of a substring in a string using the function find(). It will return the index of the first occurrence when found. Otherwise, it will return -1.

For example, given text="123abc123abc" , then text.find("abc") returns 3 because "abc" first occurs at index 3 of text.

Write a program to ask user to input a string followed by a substring. At the first occurrence of the substring in the string, replace each of those characters in the string with "-". Display the resulting string.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input

mississippi is

google g

not here there

find somewhere where

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the example below: Example 1 Enter string: mississippi Enter substring: is m--sissippi

Example 2 Enter string: google Enter substring: g -oogle

Example 3 Enter string: not here Enter substring: there not here

Example 4 Enter string: find somewhere Enter substring: where find some-----

You want to create intelligent plus and minus functions that can automatically detect if you are adding or subtracting strings or integers so that they can produce the right results.

Write a python class named NumOperation with the following attributes:

Object Variable x, y stores 2 input strings

Functions add() returns the value of x + y subtract() returns the value of x - y

Create a python class named StrOperation which inherits NumOperation and overrides the function subtract(). The function will subtract the first occurrence of string y from string x if it exists (eg. if x = "ABCDEF" and y = "CDE", then x - y = "ABF"). Otherwise, the subtraction does not change x.

Write a program that does the following: 1. Ask the user to input x and y 2. If x and y are both digits, create an object from NumOperation. Otherwise, create an object from StrOperation. 3. Call the functions add() and subtract() and display the results in the format shown in the test output.

Note that NumOperation will initialise x and y as integers whereas StrOperation will initialise them as strings when the object is created.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Hint: - recall isdigit() and find() from previous steps

Test Input

100 5

abc100 100

100abc 100

abc100abc abc

abcd cde

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the example below: Example 1 Enter x: 100 Enter y: 5 100 + 5 = 105 100 - 5 = 95

Example 2 Enter x: abc100 Enter y: 100 abc100 + 100 = abc100100 abc100 - 100 = abc

Example 3 Enter x: 100abc Enter y: 100 100abc + 100 = 100abc100 100abc - 100 = abc

Example 4 Enter x: abc100abc Enter y: abc abc100abc + abc = abc100abcabc abc100abc - abc = 100abc

Example 5 Enter x: abcd Enter y: cde abcd + cde = abcdcde abcd - cde = abcd
